title: 2026年6月英语六级听力 第1套

units.title: Conversation One
units.transcript:
M: Welcome to Business Matters. [1] Today, we have invited career development consultant Lucy Williams to talk about how to get ahead at work. Hi, Lucy. Many of us never seem to get promoted. Why is that? And what can we do about it?
W: [2] One mistake people make is to limit communication only to their bosses. It's important to expand your network and include your coworkers.
M: But some of our coworkers are less senior to us. Is it really necessary to connect with them?
W: It's important not to underestimate your colleagues. Sometimes a job title might not clearly demonstrate the influence they may have.
M: Now many of us think that working hard creates a good impression, but this isn't always true, is it?
W: That's right. We should avoid trying to take on too much work and constantly staying late just to show that you are committed.
M: I see. So setting expectations too high at the beginning can make us look bad if we don't maintain them.
W: Yeah. [3] It's better to make sure you are putting in quality time instead of just a large quantity of time. And these efforts can easily be demonstrated by the results we achieve.
M: What about helping others at work? Should you try and go beyond your normal responsibilities and offer to help people with their projects?
W: Extend your assistance to those who need it, but only as long as your own work will not go unattended. If someone can benefit from your assistance or advice, help them out to gain their respect and trust.
M: [4] But it goes without saying that you shouldn't act like a know-it-all. Otherwise, you'll appear arrogant.
W: Absolutely. Be humble. And you'll get a lot of time later on to show your genius.

questions.question_text: What are the speakers mainly talking about?
questions.question_text_zh: 对话人主要在讨论什么?

options.label: A
options.text: 如何成功经营企业

options.label: B
options.text: 如何在职业上取得进展

options.label: C
options.text: 为什么很少有人能够充分发挥自己的能力

options.label: D
options.text: 为什么年轻人很少能获得预期的晋升

questions.source_explanation:
【答案定位】答案为 B)。句[1]男士提到，今天我们邀请了职业发展顾问露西·威廉姆斯来分享如何在职场中取得成功。B) 项是对录音中 how to get ahead at work 的同义转述，故为答案。
【录音原句】[1] Today, we have invited career development consultant Lucy Williams to talk about how to get ahead at work.（今天，我们邀请了职业发展顾问露西·威廉姆斯来谈谈如何在职场中取得进步。）
🎧【连读提醒】关键短语 how to get ahead at work：how to 里 to 常弱读为 /tə/；get 词尾 /t/ 与 ahead 的元音往往连读；ahead 词尾 /d/ 常与 at 连读；at work 里 at 常弱读。抓住重读的 ahead / work 定位答案。
questions.distractor_analysis: A) 项“经营企业”在录音中未被提及，故排除；C) 项“充分发挥自己的能力”在录音中未被提及，故排除；D) 项是依据录音中 Many of us never seem to get promoted（我们中的许多人似乎从未得到晋升）设置的干扰项，但录音是泛指“许多人”，而非特指“年轻人很少获得晋升”，故排除。
questions.evidence_text: [1] Today, we have invited career development consultant Lucy Williams to talk about how to get ahead at work.

questions.question_text: What does the woman say is one mistake people make?
questions.question_text_zh: 女士说人们犯的一个错误是什么?

options.label: A
options.text: 与组织内的平级同事交流互动

options.label: B
options.text: 只和同事进行沟通

options.label: C
options.text: 只和他们的上级交流

options.label: D
options.text: 低估他们在公司中的作用

questions.source_explanation:
【答案定位】答案为 C)。句[2]女士提到，人们所犯的一个错误是只和上司沟通。C) 项是对录音中 to limit communication only to their bosses 的同义转述，故为答案。
【录音原句】W: [2] One mistake people make is to limit communication only to their bosses.（人们所犯的一个错误是只和自己的上司沟通。）
🎧【连读提醒】关键短语 limit communication only to their bosses：limit 词尾 /t/ 在后面辅音前往往不完全爆破；to their 里 to 常弱读为 /tə/、their 常弱读为 /ðə(r)/。抓住重读的 mistake / limit / bosses 定位。
questions.distractor_analysis: A) 项“与组织内的平级同事交流互动”其实是录音建议的正确做法（expand your network and include your coworkers），而本题问的是“人们所犯的错误”，A 项并非错误，故排除；B) 项是依据录音中 limit communication only to their bosses（只和上司沟通）设置的干扰项，但录音说的是只和老板交流，而不是只和同事交流，故排除；D) 项是依据录音中 underestimate your colleagues（低估同事）设置的干扰项，但录音说的是不要低估同事是很重要的，而不是低估他们在公司的作用，且这并不是女士提到的人们犯的一个错误，故排除。
questions.evidence_text: W: [2] One mistake people make is to limit communication only to their bosses.

questions.question_text: What does the woman advise people to do in their work?
questions.question_text_zh: 女士建议人们在工作中做什么?

options.label: A
options.text: 投入高质量的时间

options.label: B
options.text: 和管理者们沟通

options.label: C
options.text: 付出更多的努力

options.label: D
options.text: 展示最终的结果

questions.source_explanation:
【答案定位】答案为 A)。句[3]女士提到，与其只是投入大量时间，不如确保你投入的是高质量的时间，而非单纯追求时间总量的增加。A) 项是对录音中 putting in quality time 的同义转述，故为答案。
【录音原句】[3] It's better to make sure you are putting in quality time instead of just a large quantity of time.（更好的做法是确保你投入的是高质量的时间，而不只是大量的时间。）
🎧【连读提醒】关键短语 putting in quality time：putting 里 /t/ 在元音间美音常读作闪音 /ɾ/，词尾 /ŋ/ 与 in 往往连读；quality 里 /t/ 也常闪音化。抓住重读对比词 quality ↔ quantity 定位。
questions.distractor_analysis: 录音中女士说的是只和上级交流是人们犯的一个错误，女士并未建议和管理者们沟通，故排除 B) 项；C) 项是依据录音中 trying to take on too much work（承担过多工作）设置的干扰项，但录音中女士说的是不建议承担过多的工作，故排除；D) 项是依据录音中 demonstrated by the results（用结果来证明）设置的干扰项，但录音说的是这些努力可通过取得的结果轻松证明，而不是女士建议展示最终的结果，故排除。
questions.evidence_text: [3] It's better to make sure you are putting in quality time instead of just a large quantity of time.

questions.question_text: Why does the man say one should not act like a know-it-all?
questions.question_text_zh: 为什么男士说一个人不应该表现得像无所不知一样?

options.label: A
options.text: 为了展示他们的天赋

options.label: B
options.text: 为了赢得应有的尊重

options.label: C
options.text: 为了防止遭受羞辱

options.label: D
options.text: 为了避免显得傲慢

questions.source_explanation:
【答案定位】答案为 D)。句[4]男士提到，但不言而喻，你不应该表现得像无所不知一样，否则你会显得傲慢。D) 项是对录音中 you'll appear arrogant 的概括转述，故为答案。
【录音原句】M: [4] But it goes without saying that you shouldn't act like a know-it-all. Otherwise, you'll appear arrogant.（但不言而喻，你不应该表现得好像无所不知一样。否则，你会显得傲慢。）
🎧【连读提醒】关键短语 shouldn't act like a know-it-all：shouldn't 词尾 /t/ 与 act 的元音往往连读；act like 里 /t/ 在 /l/ 前往往不完全爆破；know-it-all 三词元音相接常连读，美音中 it 的 /t/ 常喉塞化（/ˈnoʊɪʔɔːl/）。抓住重读的 shouldn't / know-it-all 定位。
questions.distractor_analysis: A) 项是依据录音中 show your genius（展示天赋）设置的干扰项，但录音说的是要谦虚、以后有机会展示天赋，并不是不应表现得无所不知的原因，且这句话是女士说的，故排除；B) 项是依据录音中 gain their respect（赢得尊重）设置的干扰项，但录音说的是通过帮助他人从而赢得尊重，这不是不应表现得无所不知的原因，故排除；C) 项“为了防止遭受羞辱”在录音中未被提及，故排除。
questions.evidence_text: M: [4] But it goes without saying that you shouldn't act like a know-it-all. Otherwise, you'll appear arrogant.

units.title: Conversation Two
units.transcript:
W: [5] I think we first need to decide how to divide up the presentation responsibilities. From what I recall, the presentation consists of five parts, not including the introduction and conclusion. That would mean altogether we need to allocate seven parts between the two of us.
M: So we have the abstract, the background research, the project design, the results, and the discussion portions. As the abstract section only applies to the article, we needn't include it in the presentation. How would you suggest we dole out the rest?
W: How do you feel about handling the background bit? In this way, we can both discuss the part of the project that we devoted most of our time to.
M: Hold on a minute. [6] You want me, the one who did the bulk of the task, to also do the majority of the presentation? The background research, which was so meticulous, took more than a month.
W: Okay, okay, I get it. [7] Quit your moaning. I appreciate the rigorous work ethic you applied to the research, but not the sarcasm that comes up every time I mention it. What do you think would be a fair arrangement?
M: I think the best arrangement would be to split the research into two parts: before 1980, and afterward. I will take the before portion and you would be assigned the after 1980, leaving the project and results. I volunteered to describe the project, but as I struggled a bit with the statistics in the results section, how about you handling that?
W: That's agreeable to me. I propose we both handle the discussion section in parts along with the question and answer afterward, leaving only the introduction and conclusion.
M: I will take responsibility for the conclusion and put you in charge of the introduction. [8] This will make it so that we alternate presenting so as to avoid sounding monotonous to the audience.

questions.question_text: What does the woman say they first need to do?
questions.question_text_zh: 女士表示他们首先需要做什么?

options.label: A
options.text: 决定如何分配演示任务

options.label: B
options.text: 调查现有的背景研究

options.label: C
options.text: 共同完成项目设计

options.label: D
options.text: 为他们的论文找一个合适的题目

questions.source_explanation:
【答案定位】答案为 A)。句[5]女士提到，她认为他们首先需要决定如何分配演示任务。A) 项是对录音中 divide up the presentation responsibilities 的同义转述，故为答案。
【录音原句】W: [5] I think we first need to decide how to divide up the presentation responsibilities.（我认为我们首先需要决定如何分配演示汇报的任务。）
🎧【连读提醒】关键短语 divide up the presentation responsibilities：how to 里 to 常弱读为 /tə/；divide 词尾 /d/ 与 up 往往连读。抓住重读的 first / divide up / responsibilities 定位“首先要做的事”。
questions.distractor_analysis: B) 项是依据录音中 background research（背景研究）设置的干扰项，但录音中男士提到他已经花了一个月完成背景研究，可知首先要做的并不是调查背景研究，故排除；C) 项是依据录音中 project design（项目设计）设置的干扰项，但“项目设计”只是演示内容的一个部分，而不是他们首先要做的事，故排除；D) 项“找合适的题目”在录音中未被提及，故排除。
questions.evidence_text: W: [5] I think we first need to decide how to divide up the presentation responsibilities.

questions.question_text: Why does the man refuse to handle the background part?
questions.question_text_zh: 男士为何拒绝处理背景部分?

options.label: A
options.text: 他想将时间投入到其他部分

options.label: B
options.text: 他认为女士能更好地处理背景部分

options.label: C
options.text: 他声称自己已经完成大部分工作

options.label: D
options.text: 他认为女士在细节上更加细致

questions.source_explanation:
【答案定位】答案为 C)。句[6]男士提到，你意思是让我这个承担了大部分工作任务的人，再承担大部分的演示汇报？背景研究那么细致，花了一个多月的时间呢。C) 项是对录音中 the one who did the bulk of the task 的同义转述，故为答案。
【录音原句】[6] You want me, the one who did the bulk of the task, to also do the majority of the presentation?（你想让我这个承担了大部分工作的人，再去做大部分的演示汇报？）
🎧【连读提醒】关键短语 the one who did the bulk of the task：did the 里 /d/ 在 /ð/ 前常弱化同化；bulk 词尾 /k/ 与 of 往往连读；of the 里 of 常弱读为 /əv/。抓住重读的 bulk / task / majority 定位。
questions.distractor_analysis: “将时间投入到其他部分”在录音中未被提及，故排除 A) 项；“女士能更好地处理背景部分”在录音中未被提及，故排除 B) 项；D) 项是依据录音中 meticulous（细致的）一词设置的干扰项，但录音提到的是背景研究非常细致，并不是女士更加细致，故排除。
questions.evidence_text: [6] You want me, the one who did the bulk of the task, to also do the majority of the presentation?

questions.question_text: What does the woman urge the man to stop doing?
questions.question_text_zh: 女士敦促男士停止做什么?

options.label: A
options.text: 质疑

options.label: B
options.text: 抱怨

options.label: C
options.text: 争论

options.label: D
options.text: 担心

questions.source_explanation:
【答案定位】答案为 B)。句[7]女士提到，请别再抱怨了。B) 项是对录音中 moaning 的同义转述，故为答案。
【录音原句】[7] Quit your moaning.（别再抱怨了。）
🎧【连读提醒】关键短语 Quit your moaning：quit + your 里 /t/ 与 /j/ 常同化，读作 /kwɪtʃər/。句子短，抓住重读的 quit / moaning 即可，moaning（抱怨）是解题词。
questions.distractor_analysis: A)、C)、D) 项在录音中均未被提及，故均排除。
questions.evidence_text: [7] Quit your moaning.

questions.question_text: Why does the man suggest he present the conclusion and the woman do the introduction?
questions.question_text_zh: 为什么男士建议自己负责结论部分，女士负责引言?

options.label: A
options.text: 为了避免让听众觉得内容单调乏味

options.label: B
options.text: 为了使劳动分工更加合理

options.label: C
options.text: 为了避免让自己负担过重

options.label: D
options.text: 为了充分发挥他们的能力

questions.source_explanation:
【答案定位】答案为 A)。句[8]男士提到，这可使我们交替呈现内容，从而避免让观众觉得内容单调乏味。A) 项是对录音中 to avoid sounding monotonous to the audience 的同义转述，故为答案。
【录音原句】[8] This will make it so that we alternate presenting so as to avoid sounding monotonous to the audience.（这样一来，我们就能交替演示，从而避免让听众觉得单调乏味。）
🎧【连读提醒】关键短语 avoid sounding monotonous to the audience：avoid 词尾 /d/ 在 /s/ 前常弱化、不完全爆破；to the 里 to 常弱读为 /tə/。抓住重读的 avoid / monotonous / audience 定位目的。
questions.distractor_analysis: 二人实现分工均衡是整场对话的整体诉求，而非分配引言和结论这两个部分的直接目的，故排除 B) 项；C)、D) 项在录音中均未被提及，故均排除。
questions.evidence_text: [8] This will make it so that we alternate presenting so as to avoid sounding monotonous to the audience.

units.title: Passage One
units.transcript:
Makeup can do more than just change your appearance.
[9] It can also alter others' perceptions of you, for better or for worse. According to new research from the University of Stirling in Scotland, although both men and women perceive women who wear makeup as being of a higher status, men associate makeup with prestigious positive qualities, while women view other women wearing makeup as being dominant and a potential threat.
[10] The research showed that men and women both rated the faces with cosmetics as being more attractive, but only women rated made-up faces as being more dominant, while only men rated made-up faces as being higher in prestige.
A follow-up study investigated the root cause behind these differences in perception, and found that female-on-female jealousy seemed to be the main cause for the differences in perception.
Women rating women with makeup said they would be more jealous of them and thought they would be more attractive to men than their non-make-up-wearing counterparts.
Cosmetic products are good for more than just giving you a pretty face. It can be particularly useful for women to understand how wearing makeup alters others' perceptions of them in situations where they are trying to gain others' trust and admiration.
[11] At a job interview, knowing whether the hiring committee will consist of men or women might influence a female candidate's decision about wearing makeup. Whether the interviewers will view her as attractive, dominant and prestigious, can affect the interviewers' actions and perhaps the outcome of the interview itself.

questions.question_text: What can makeup do according to new research from the University of Stirling in Scotland?
questions.question_text_zh: 根据苏格兰斯特灵大学的最新研究，化妆能起什么作用?

options.label: A
options.text: 改变他人对化妆者的看法

options.label: B
options.text: 赢得他人对化妆者的钦佩

options.label: C
options.text: 增加化妆者的自信

options.label: D
options.text: 改变化妆者的外表

questions.source_explanation:
【答案定位】答案为 A)。句[9]提到，它还可能改变他人对你的看法，这种影响可能是更好的，也可能是更坏的。A) 项是对录音中 alter others' perceptions of you 的同义转述，故为答案。
【录音原句】[9] It can also alter others' perceptions of you, for better or for worse.（它还可能改变他人对你的看法，或好或坏。）
🎧【连读提醒】关键短语 alter others' perceptions of you：alter 词尾 /r/（美音）与 others 的元音往往连读；perceptions 词尾在 /n/ 后浊化为 /z/，与 of 往往连读（/pərˈsɛpʃənz əv/）；of you 里 of 常弱读为 /əv/。抓住重读的 alter / perceptions 定位。
questions.distractor_analysis: B) 项是依据录音中 gain others' trust and admiration（赢得他人信任与钦佩）设置的干扰项，但录音说的是对女性而言了解化妆如何影响他人看法可能特别有用，而不是化妆本身的作用，故排除；C) 项“增加自信”在录音中未被提及，故排除；D) 项是依据 change your appearance（改变外表）设置的干扰项，但这并不是斯特灵大学研究结果所表明的化妆的作用，不符合题意，故排除。
questions.evidence_text: [9] It can also alter others' perceptions of you, for better or for worse.

questions.question_text: How did both men and women rate the faces with cosmetics in the new research?
questions.question_text_zh: 在新研究中，男性和女性如何对化妆后的面部形象进行评价?

options.label: A
options.text: 更具威胁性

options.label: B
options.text: 具有更高的声望

options.label: C
options.text: 更具主导性

options.label: D
options.text: 更具吸引力

questions.source_explanation:
【答案定位】答案为 D)。句[10]提到，研究显示，男性和女性均认为使用化妆品修饰后的面部更具吸引力。D) 项是对录音中 as being more attractive 的原词复现，故为答案。
【录音原句】[10] The research showed that men and women both rated the faces with cosmetics as being more attractive, but only women rated made-up faces as being more dominant, while only men rated made-up faces as being higher in prestige.（研究显示，男性和女性都认为化了妆的面孔更具吸引力，但只有女性认为化妆的面孔更具支配感，而只有男性认为化妆的面孔更具声望。）
🎧【连读提醒】关键短语 rated the faces ... as being more attractive：men and women 里 and 常弱读为 /ən/；rated the 里 /d/ 在 /ð/ 前常弱化；more 词尾 /r/（美音）与 attractive 往往连读。注意区分 both（男女都）↔ only women / only men 三个重读对比定位。
questions.distractor_analysis: A)、C) 项是依据录音中 being dominant and a potential threat（更具主导性且是潜在威胁）设置的干扰项，但这仅是女性的看法，并非男女都持有，故均排除；B) 项是依据 as being higher in prestige（更具声望）设置的干扰项，但这仅是男性的观点，并非男女双方都持有，故排除。
questions.evidence_text: [10] The research showed that men and women both rated the faces with cosmetics as being more attractive, but only women rated made-up faces as being more dominant, while only men rated made-up faces as being higher in prestige.

questions.question_text: Why does a female candidate need to know the gender of the hiring committee members?
questions.question_text_zh: 为什么女性候选人需要了解招聘委员会成员的性别?

options.label: A
options.text: 这可能会影响她介绍自己的方式

options.label: B

units.title: Passage Two
units.transcript:
[12] You may have seen advertisements trumpeting methods of changing a habit that require absolutely no willpower whatsoever.
But can you really change a bad habit or create a good one without willpower? To answer this question, we first have to ask: what is willpower?
Most people, sadly, think of it only as the ability to clench their teeth and resist attractive temptations. In this view, willpower means self-denial and no fun. No wonder people hope to make changes without it.
[13] I define willpower as using only the thought of your motivators to control your actions. Let's say your motivators are preventing diabetes and reaching a healthy weight.
So if you are at the all-you-can-eat buffet, you think about your motivator: avoid diabetes through weight loss. And you take small portions and avoid the dessert table.
[14] So amazingly enough, willpower begins with a thought- a bright idea, some way to improve your life or contribute to others. This bright idea is your motivator.
Dr. Walter Mitchell, an expert on willpower skills, uses the expressive term " a burning goal". Whether you call it a motivator, a burning goal, or a bright idea, this idea is the force behind your willpower.
[15] What sort of bright ideas, motivators, make for effective willpower? In fact, any goal that you value strongly counts.
The list may include good health, self-respect, a better future for your family, personal mission and being a role model for your child. All these can certainly drive a positive change.

units.title: Recording One
units.transcript:
For many pregnant women, understanding what seafood is safe and healthy and what should be avoided because of mercury concerns comes with a lot of worrying.
[16] In part, that's because the federal government's advice on the matter first issued in 2004 has long been criticized as vague.
[17-1] That guidance has included advice on how much seafood to eat and which species pregnant and breast-feeding women should avoid over concerns about mercury contamination.
But critics say the government advisory has done more harm than good, scaring many pregnant and breast-feeding women away from eating seafood altogether. The problem is real.
According to a spokesman for the Food and Drug Administration or FDA for short, the agency analyzed fish consumption data from more than 1, 000 pregnant women in the U.S. and found that 21 % of them ate no fish whatsoever in the previous month.
And those who did eat fish consumed far less than recommended by the dietary guidelines. Some 50% ate less than 2 ounces a week and 75% ate less than 4 ounces.
[17-2] This week, the FDA issued an update to the advice, listing more than 60 species in a chart that ranks fish as a best choice, good choice and choices to avoid.
The goal is to make it easier for mothers-to-be to feel confident about the type of seafood they include in their diets.
The new advice recommends consumers choose a variety of fish to eat and it comes with an easy-to-understand illustration of what an appropriate portion size should be: 4 ounces for an adult and 2 ounces for children aged 4 to 7.
And while expectant mothers have long been warned to stay away from shark and four other particular types of fish from the Gulf of Mexico, now there are three new species on the list of what to avoid.
But not everyone is thrilled with the new advice. Critics say the new advice doesn't always agree with the agency's own scientific findings.
[18] While mercury is a great concern when people are talking about pregnant women and seafood, it's not the only factor contributing to anxiety. The FDA maintains that its final consumption recommendations were based on thorough scientific analysis.
Agency spokesman Cassell says the FDA believes the recommendations will increase confidence, not uncertainty. But critics disagree. They think the FDA's advice is not based on the evidence in its own detailed report, and so it confuses everyone.

units.title: Recording Two
units.transcript:
I know you're busy with work, but you also need to take some time off to recharge those batteries. So, should you plan one big vacation for the year? Or Should you take multiple short vacations throughout?
Quantity can sometimes beat quality. First and foremost, regardless of how you use your vacation days, you need to be using them, and soon.
The longer you put off your time off, the worse you're making things for yourself. One 9-year-long study published in Psychosomatic Medicine suggests not taking at least one vacation a year may increase your risk of mortality due to heart disease.
[19] So, not only are you killing your joy, you're possibly killing yourself. Give yourself a break, folks. When you should take those breaks, however, depends on a few factors: how many days you have available to use, what activities bring you joy, whether you have a family or not, and other variables come into play.
Because of that, there's no perfect formula that works for everyone, but there are still a few things everyone can try to shoot for.
We know that in terms of maximizing relaxation, you should aim for vacations that range somewhere between 7 and 11 days long. That gives you enough time to let go of your stress at work, completely loosen up and achieve full-on calm.
[20] That above-mentioned study also recommends you space out your vacations evenly instead of using up all of your days at once. 8 days might sound like a lot for someone who only gets 10 days of vacation a year. But if you frame them with weekends, you can manage two evenly spaced 8-day vacations a year.
If you have 14 days of paid leave, that's almost three separate 8-day vacations you can use to split your year into thirds. As tempting as it might be to use all your days to take one long summer break, your overall goal should be to achieve the perfect balance between length plus joy and frequency.
[21] Vacation frequency is important because planning multiple breaks throughout the year means you always have something to look forward to.
Planning things and the anticipation that comes with it tends to make us happier. If you only take one long vacation every year, the excitement builds much more slowly and seems so far off that it can actually lead to feelings of despair.

【录音原句】[19] So, not only are you killing your joy, you're possibly killing yourself.（所以，你不仅在扼杀自己的快乐，还可能在毁掉自己（的健康）。）
🎧【连读提醒】关键短语 not only are you killing your joy：not only 里 /t/ 后接元音，常喉塞化（/ʔ/）；are 常弱读为 /ər/，与 you 顺读；killing 词尾读 /ŋ/（-ing），与 your 的 /j/ 相接顺读（非 C+V 连读）。抓住重读的 not only ... joy / yourself 这组递进对比定位。
questions.distractor_analysis: A) 项“很快崩溃”在录音中并未提及，故排除；C) 项“使家人面临风险”在录音中未提及，故排除；D) 项是依据录音中 the worse you're making things for yourself 设置的干扰项，但录音说的是使你自己的处境变得更糟，而不是周围的人，故排除。
questions.evidence_text: [19] So, not only are you killing your joy, you're possibly killing yourself.

questions.question_text: What does the 9-year study recommend people do when planning vacations?
questions.question_text_zh: 这项为期9年的研究建议人们在规划假期时采取什么措施?

options.label: A
options.text: 每年安排14天的假期

options.label: B
options.text: 每年计划安排三次独立的假期

options.label: C
options.text: 均匀分布假期，而不是只休一次长假

options.label: D
options.text: 攒下所有假期休个长长的暑假，彻底放松身心

questions.source_explanation:
【答案定位】答案为 C)。句[20]提到，上述研究还建议你均匀分布假期，而非一次性用完所有假期天数。其中 That above-mentioned study 指的是前文提到的发表于《身心医学》的 9 年研究。C) 项是对录音中 space out your vacations evenly instead of using up all of your days at once 的同义转述，故为答案。
【录音原句】[20] That above-mentioned study also recommends you space out your vacations evenly instead of using up all of your days at once. 8 days might sound like a lot for someone who only gets 10 days of vacation a year.（上述那项研究还建议你把假期均匀地分散开，而不是一次性用完所有假期。对于一年只有 10 天假期的人来说，8 天可能听起来很多。）
🎧【连读提醒】关键短语 space out your vacations evenly：space 词尾 /s/ 与 out 往往连读成 /speɪs aʊt/；out your 里 /t/ 与 /j/ 常同化成 /aʊtʃər/；all of 往往连读成 /ɔːl əv/。抓住重读的 space out / evenly / instead 定位“均匀分散”。
questions.distractor_analysis: A) 项是依据录音中 14 days of paid leave 设置的干扰项，但录音说的是“如果你有 14 天带薪假”，这只是一个假设的例子，并非研究强制要求的标准天数，故排除；B) 项是依据录音中 three separate 8-day vacations 设置的干扰项，但录音说的是如果刚好有 14 天带薪年假差不多可分成三个 8 天假期，这只是特定条件下的推算，不是普遍适用的建议，故排除；D) 项是依据录音中 full-on calm 和 use all your days to take one long summer break 设置的干扰项，但录音说的是尽管把所有假期攒起来一次性休完长假很诱人，整体目标应达到长度、愉悦和频率的完美平衡，研究本身不建议一次性用完假期，故排除。
questions.evidence_text: [20] That above-mentioned study also recommends you space out your vacations evenly instead of using up all of your days at once. 8 days might sound like a lot for someone who only gets 10 days of vacation a year.

questions.question_text: Why is vacation frequency important according to the speaker?
questions.question_text_zh: 根据讲话者的观点，休假频率为何非常重要?

options.label: A
options.text: 期待一年中有更多的假期会提高工作效率

options.label: B
options.text: 期待更多假期会减少工作中的绝望感

options.label: C
options.text: 每年休三次以上的假能延长兴奋感

options.label: D
options.text: 全年规划多次休息时间能提升幸福感

questions.source_explanation:
【答案定位】答案为 D)。句[21]提到，休假频率至关重要，因为全年安排多次假期意味着你总会有值得期待的事情，制定计划以及随之而来的期待感往往能让我们更快乐。D) 项是对录音中 planning multiple breaks throughout the year 和 make us happier 的同义转述，故为答案。
【录音原句】[21] Vacation frequency is important because planning multiple breaks throughout the year means you always have something to look forward to. Planning things and the anticipation that comes with it tends to make us happier.（假期的频率很重要，因为在全年安排多次休假意味着你总有可以期待的事情。制定计划以及随之而来的期待感，往往能让我们更快乐。）
🎧【连读提醒】关键短语 you always have something to look forward to：look 词尾 /k/ 在 forward 的 /f/ 前往往不完全爆破；forward to、something to 里 to 常弱读为 /tə/。抓住重读的 frequency / multiple breaks / look forward to 定位。
questions.distractor_analysis: A) 项“提高工作效率”在录音中未被提及，故排除；B) 项在录音中未被提及，故排除；录音中仅提到全年多次休息能提升幸福感，并未强调为“三次以上”，故排除 C) 项。
questions.evidence_text: [21] Vacation frequency is important because planning multiple breaks throughout the year means you always have something to look forward to. Planning things and the anticipation that comes with it tends to make us happier.

units.title: Recording Three
units.transcript:
Autonomous cars that can take over from drivers if they are tired or caught in the heat of an argument are being developed in Sweden.
[22] Researchers working as part of the European Union's 87 billion research program are developing sensor-based systems that monitor whether a driver is distracted, anxious or tired. If a driver is not in a fit state to be on the road, the car automatically takes control of the wheel to prevent accidents.
Dr. Anna Anund from the Swedish National Road and Transport Research Institute, who is leading the project, said a driver's state can be measured using a number of sensors, including heart rate monitors and eye sensors, which track where a driver's gaze is.
[23] She said the aim was to really make sure that the transition from the driver to the vehicle is done in a safe way, so we can take into consideration the driver's state, and so we do not give control to a driver who is under pressure of fatigue, stress, anxiety, and so on.
According to data from the European Commission, Sweden has the safest roads in the EU, with the UK a close second. However, the number of road accidents in both has largely leveled out since 2010.
[24] Driver fatigue is thought to be responsible for as many as a fifth of road crashes across the EU.
Although there are certain times of the day when more accidents happen- at 6 am, for example, drivers are said to be 20 times more likely to have an accident than at 10 am. While most experts agree driverless technology should help bring down accident numbers in the long term, some have questioned whether it is safe.
The researchers have said the technology they are developing is seeking to bridge the gap between Level 3 on the autonomy scale in which drivers have to be ready to take control of the car at any point, and Level 4 in which driving is automated.
Daniel Ruiz, the chief executive of the UK's Connected and Autonomous Vehicle Program Meridian, said there is a strong debate going on about how it is possible to make a Level 3 car completely safe. Despite advances in technology, we still have some way to go in shifting public sentiment.
[25] With an increase in attention-grabbing accidents recently, drivers now view self-driving cars as less safe than they used to.

questions.question_text: What are researchers doing in Sweden?
questions.question_text_zh: 研究人员在瑞典正在开展什么工作?

options.label: A
options.text: 调查驾驶员何时陷入激烈的争吵中

options.label: B
options.text: 设计设备以防止驾驶员分心

options.label: C
options.text: 测试用于监测驾驶员容易疲劳的模型

options.label: D
options.text: 开发基于传感器的自动驾驶车辆系统

questions.source_explanation:
【答案定位】答案为 D)。句[22]提到，参与欧盟 870 亿欧元研究计划的研究人员正在开发基于传感器的系统，用于监测驾驶员是否分心、焦虑或疲劳。D) 项是对录音中 developing sensor-based systems 的原词复现，故为答案。
【录音原句】[22] Researchers working as part of the European Union's 87 billion research program are developing sensor-based systems that monitor whether a driver is distracted, anxious or tired.（作为欧盟 870 亿研究计划一部分的研究人员，正在开发基于传感器的系统，用于监测驾驶员是否分心、焦虑或疲劳。）
🎧【连读提醒】关键短语 monitor whether a driver is distracted, anxious or tired：part 词尾 /t/ 与 of 往往连读成 /pɑːrɾ əv/；whether 词尾 /r/（美音）与 a 往往连读；anxious 词尾 /s/ 与 or 往往连读。抓住重读的 sensor / monitor / distracted / tired 定位系统功能。
questions.distractor_analysis: A) 项是依据原文中 caught in the heat of an argument 设置的干扰项，但录音说的是新系统能够应对的一种驾驶状态，并不是说研究人员去调查人们吵架的时间点，故排除；B) 项是依据原文中 driver is distracted 设置的干扰项，但录音说这些传感器系统是用来监测驾驶员是否分心或疲劳的，而不是用来防止他们分心的，故排除；C) 项“容易疲劳”在录音中未提及，故排除。
questions.evidence_text: [22] Researchers working as part of the European Union's 87 billion research program are developing sensor-based systems that monitor whether a driver is distracted, anxious or tired.

questions.question_text: What did the researchers' project aim to do according to Dr. Anna Anund?
questions.question_text_zh: 据安娜·阿努德博士介绍，研究人员在该项目中旨在实现什么目标?

options.label: A
options.text: 确保自动驾驶车辆以最简单的方式运行

options.label: B
options.text: 确保从驾驶员到车辆的过渡过程安全完成

options.label: C
options.text: 尽可能减轻驾驶员的压力

options.label: D
options.text: 尽可能准确地记录驾驶员的状态

questions.source_explanation:
【答案定位】答案为 B)。句[23]提到，她表示，目标是真正确保从驾驶员到车辆的过渡过程以安全方式进行，从而能够考虑驾驶员的状态。B) 项是对录音中 make sure that the transition from the driver to the vehicle is done in a safe way 的同义转述，故为答案。
【录音原句】[23] She said the aim was to really make sure that the transition from the driver to the vehicle is done in a safe way, so we can take into consideration the driver's state, and so we do not give control to a driver who is under pressure of fatigue, stress, anxiety, and so on.（她说，目的是要真正确保从驾驶员到车辆的控制权交接以安全的方式完成，以便我们能把驾驶员的状态纳入考虑，从而不把控制权交给正处于疲劳、压力、焦虑等状态下的驾驶员。）
🎧【连读提醒】关键短语 the transition from the driver to the vehicle is done in a safe way：make 词尾 /k/ 在 sure 的 /ʃ/ 前往往不完全爆破；take 词尾 /k/ 与 into 往往连读，into 常弱读为 /ɪntə/；done in a 往往连读成 /dʌn ɪn ə/。抓住重读的 transition / safe way / driver's state 定位“安全交接”。
questions.distractor_analysis: A) 项“最简单的方式”在录音中未提及，故排除；录音中提到系统会考虑驾驶员在疲劳、压力或焦虑下的状态，目的是防止把控制权交给这种状态下的他们，而不是 C) 项“减轻”他们的压力，故排除；D) 项是依据录音中 driver's state 设置的干扰项，录音说的是使用传感器来检测驾驶员的状态，但这只是手段，并不是该项目要实现的最终目标，故排除。
questions.evidence_text: [23] She said the aim was to really make sure that the transition from the driver to the vehicle is done in a safe way, so we can take into consideration the driver's state, and so we do not give control to a driver who is under pressure of fatigue, stress, anxiety, and so on.

questions.question_text: What is thought to be responsible for a fifth of road accidents across the European Union?
questions.question_text_zh: 什么被认为是欧盟五分之一事故的原因?

options.label: A
options.text: 驾驶员疲劳

options.label: B
options.text: 糟糕的交通状况

options.label: C
options.text: 酒后驾驶

options.label: D
options.text: 驾驶时间

questions.source_explanation:
【答案定位】答案为 A)。句[24]提到，驾驶员疲劳被认为是导致欧盟范围内多达五分之一交通事故的原因。A) 项是对录音中 Driver fatigue 的原词复现，故为答案。
【录音原句】[24] Driver fatigue is thought to be responsible for as many as a fifth of road crashes across the EU.（据认为，驾驶员疲劳是欧盟境内多达五分之一的道路交通事故的原因。）
🎧【连读提醒】关键短语 responsible for as many as a fifth of road crashes：thought to 里 to 常弱读为 /tə/；as、for 常弱读，as a 往往连读；fifth 词尾 /θ/ 与 of 往往连读成 /fɪfθ əv/。抓住重读的 fatigue / responsible / a fifth 定位比例。
questions.distractor_analysis: B) 项“糟糕的交通状况”在录音中未提及，故排除；C) 项“酒后驾驶”在录音中未提及，故排除；录音中虽然提到早上 6 点发生事故的概率是上午 10 点的 20 倍，但这只是说明疲劳高发的时间段，并不是说 D) 项“驾驶时间”导致了五分之一的事故，故排除。
questions.evidence_text: [24] Driver fatigue is thought to be responsible for as many as a fifth of road crashes across the EU.

questions.question_text: Why do drivers now view self-driving cars as less safe than they used to?
questions.question_text_zh: 为什么如今司机们认为自动驾驶汽车比过去更不安全?

options.label: A
options.text: 关于三级自动驾驶汽车的可行性一直存在激烈争论

options.label: B
options.text: 汽车技术方面几乎没有显著的进步

options.label: C
options.text: 近期引人关注的事故数量有所增加

options.label: D
options.text: 改变公众情绪的可行方法很少

questions.source_explanation:
【答案定位】答案为 C)。句[25]提到，随着近期引人关注的交通事故频发，如今驾驶员普遍认为自动驾驶汽车的安全性低于以往水平。C) 项是对录音中 With an increase in attention-grabbing accidents recently 的同义转述，故为答案。
【录音原句】[25] With an increase in attention-grabbing accidents recently, drivers now view self-driving cars as less safe than they used to.（由于近来引人注目的事故有所增加，驾驶员如今认为自动驾驶汽车不如以往那么安全了。）
🎧【连读提醒】关键短语 view self-driving cars as less safe than they used to：With an 往往连读成 /wɪð ən/；increase 词尾 /s/ 与 in 往往连读；than 常弱读为 /ðən/；used to 里 /d/ 与 /t/ 合并读 /juːstə/。抓住重读的 less safe / than they used to 定位“不如以往安全”。
questions.distractor_analysis: A) 项是依据录音中 strong debate 和 Level 3 car 设置的干扰项，录音说的是专家提到对三级汽车的安全性有激烈辩论，但这只是背景信息，并非公众觉得“自动驾驶汽车比过去不安全”的直接原因，故排除；录音中明确提到技术取得了进步（advances），而不是 B) 项“没有显著的进步”，故排除；D) 项是依据录音中 some way to go in shifting public sentiment 设置的干扰项，但录音说的是改变公众情绪方面还有很长的路要走，并非“可行的方法很少”，故排除。
questions.evidence_text: [25] With an increase in attention-grabbing accidents recently, drivers now view self-driving cars as less safe than they used to.
